steps.label: Cortex and white matter
steps.detail: Name the side, lobe, gyrus or sulcus and cortical, subcortical or deep white matter position.
steps.look: Axial images with sagittal confirmation; find the central sulcus (hand knob, pars marginalis) to separate frontal from parietal lobes.
findings: [Right] [precentral gyrus], cortical and subcortical, anterior to the central sulcus.
Deep white matter of the [left] centrum semiovale.
steps.tip: The hand knob of the precentral gyrus and the pars marginalis of the cingulate sulcus identify the central sulcus.

steps.label: Deep grey matter and capsules
steps.detail: Localise to the caudate, lentiform nucleus, thalamus, internal capsule limb or corpus callosum segment.
steps.look: Axial images at the level of the foramen of Monro and the thalamus; coronal images.
findings: Posterior limb of the [left] internal capsule.
Splenium of the corpus callosum.
[Right] thalamus (posterolateral).

steps.label: Brainstem and cerebellum
steps.detail: Localise to midbrain, pons or medulla, and cerebellar hemisphere, vermis or peduncle.
steps.look: Sagittal and axial images of the posterior fossa; relation to the fourth ventricle.
findings: [Left] paramedian pons.
[Right] middle cerebellar peduncle.
Cerebellar vermis.

steps.label: Ventricles, cisterns and midline
steps.detail: Trace ventricles, cisterns, extra-axial spaces and the midline.
steps.look: Ventricular size and symmetry; basal cisterns; midline structures.
steps.normal: Ventricles, cisterns and extra-axial spaces normal; midline central.
findings: Midline shift of __ mm to the [left] at the level of the septum pellucidum.
Effacement of the [right] ambient cistern.

steps.label: Vascular territory
steps.detail: Relate the finding to arterial territories, border zones or venous drainage, allowing for variation.
steps.look: Territory maps: ACA medial, MCA lateral, PCA occipital and medial temporal; lenticulostriate deep territory; border zones between them.
findings: Distribution corresponds to the [left MCA] territory.
Internal border-zone (watershed) distribution.
Distribution does not follow an arterial territory (consider venous or non-vascular causes).
steps.tip: Arterial territory boundaries vary between individuals; a lesion crossing territories needs a wider differential.

steps.label: Parenchyma and ASPECTS
steps.detail: Look for early ischaemic change and localise it by side, territory and strategic structures; give ASPECTS when applicable.
steps.look: Narrow window width (about 30–40 HU) on non-contrast CT: insular ribbon, lentiform nucleus and cortex; DWI with ADC on MRI.
steps.normal: No acute ischaemic change; ASPECTS 10.
findings: Loss of the insular ribbon and obscuration of the [left] lentiform nucleus; ASPECTS __ (regions [ ]).
Established hypoattenuation in the [right] MCA territory.
Restricted diffusion in the [ ] with low ADC (acute infarct).
steps.tip: A normal early CT does not exclude infarction; subtle loss of grey–white differentiation needs a narrow window.

steps.label: Haemorrhage
steps.detail: Exclude intracranial haemorrhage in every compartment before treatment decisions.
steps.look: Parenchyma, subarachnoid spaces, ventricles and extra-axial spaces on non-contrast CT or susceptibility MRI.
steps.normal: No intracranial haemorrhage.
findings: Acute intraparenchymal haemorrhage in the [ ].
Haemorrhagic transformation of the infarct [petechial / parenchymal haematoma].
Subarachnoid haemorrhage in the [ ].

steps.label: Arterial occlusion
steps.detail: Name the occluded artery and segment, tandem cervical disease and distal reconstitution.
steps.look: CTA from the arch to the vertex; dense artery sign on non-contrast CT.
steps.normal: No large-vessel occlusion; cervical and intracranial arteries patent.
findings: Occlusion of the [left] M1 segment of the MCA (dense MCA sign on non-contrast CT).
Tandem occlusion: [right] ICA origin and M1.
Basilar artery occlusion.
Cervical ICA dissection with tapered narrowing.
steps.tip: Look at the cervical arteries too: a tandem ICA lesion changes the endovascular approach.

steps.label: Collaterals and perfusion
steps.detail: Describe collateral filling and, when valid, perfusion core and hypoperfused tissue volumes with the software used.
steps.look: Multiphase CTA for delayed collateral filling; perfusion maps checked for motion, bolus and coverage.
steps.normal: Perfusion not acquired.
findings: Good collaterals: filling of more than half of the territory with a one-phase delay.
Poor collaterals with minimal filling.
Perfusion ([software], thresholds [ ]): core __ mL, hypoperfused tissue __ mL, mismatch volume __ mL.
steps.tip: Single-phase CTA underestimates delayed collaterals; treatment selection follows the clinical pathway, not a single number.

steps.label: Mass effect and alternative findings
steps.detail: Report oedema, midline shift, cisterns, hydrocephalus and any alternative diagnosis.
steps.look: Midline, basal cisterns and fourth ventricle (for cerebellar infarcts).
steps.normal: No mass effect; no alternative cause for the symptoms.
findings: Malignant oedema with __ mm midline shift and effacement of the basal cisterns.
Cerebellar infarct compressing the fourth ventricle with early hydrocephalus.
Stroke mimic: [tumour / subdural haematoma].

steps.label: Location and compartment
steps.detail: Identify intra-axial, extra-axial, intraventricular or skull-base origin and all involved compartments.
steps.look: Multiplanar images: a CSF cleft, dural tail and buckled grey matter indicate an extra-axial lesion.
findings: Solitary intra-axial lesion centred in the [right] [frontal] white matter, __ × __ × __ mm.
Extra-axial dural-based mass with a CSF cleft and dural tail (meningioma pattern).
Multiple lesions at the grey–white junction (metastases pattern).
steps.tip: First decide intra- or extra-axial; the differential is completely different.

steps.label: Signal and enhancement
steps.detail: Separate enhancing solid tissue, non-enhancing signal abnormality, necrosis, cyst, haemorrhage and calcification.
steps.look: T1, T2/FLAIR, susceptibility and post-contrast T1 in matching planes.
findings: Thick irregular ring enhancement around central necrosis with surrounding FLAIR signal.
Non-enhancing T2/FLAIR-hyperintense expansile lesion.
Homogeneously enhancing dural-based mass.
Cyst with an enhancing mural nodule.

steps.label: Diffusion and perfusion
steps.detail: Describe diffusion and, when acquired, perfusion and spectroscopy in the viable component.
steps.look: DWI/ADC of the solid part and cavity; perfusion rCBV in the enhancing rim.
findings: Restricted diffusion in the solid component (highly cellular tumour, e.g., lymphoma).
Restricted diffusion in the cavity with a smooth thin rim (abscess pattern).
Elevated rCBV in the enhancing rim.
steps.tip: Restricted diffusion in a cavity favours abscess; restricted diffusion in solid tissue suggests a cellular tumour.

steps.label: Extent and dissemination
steps.detail: Assess corpus callosum, deep nuclei and brainstem involvement, dural or skull invasion and ventricular or leptomeningeal spread.
steps.look: Coronal and sagittal post-contrast images; ependymal and leptomeningeal surfaces.
steps.normal: No callosal, ventricular or leptomeningeal involvement; no additional lesions.
findings: Extension across the corpus callosum to the contralateral hemisphere.
Subependymal enhancement along the ventricles.
Leptomeningeal enhancement in the [ ].

steps.label: Oedema and pressure effect
steps.detail: Report vasogenic oedema, midline shift, cisterns and obstructive hydrocephalus.
steps.look: FLAIR extent; midline at the septum pellucidum; ventricular size.
steps.normal: No significant oedema, mass effect or hydrocephalus.
findings: Vasogenic oedema with __ mm midline shift.
Subfalcine herniation.
Obstructive hydrocephalus at the level of the [foramen of Monro / fourth ventricle].

steps.label: Treatment comparison
steps.detail: Compare the same components with the named baseline and describe treatment effect versus progression.
steps.look: Matched planes and sequences with the post-operative baseline or nadir.
steps.normal: No prior treatment; not applicable.
findings: Stable enhancing and non-enhancing components compared with [date].
New enhancing nodule at the resection margin (progression versus treatment effect).
Enhancement within the radiation field with low rCBV, favouring treatment effect.
steps.tip: Name the reference study and measure the same component each time.

model.reporting_aim: Follow each common and internal carotid artery from the bifurcation to the skull base before grading narrowing.

steps.label: Site and morphology
steps.detail: Identify the side, segment and morphology of narrowing or wall abnormality.
steps.look: CTA or contrast MRA source images and curved reformats along each carotid; Doppler when performed.
steps.normal: Carotid arteries patent without significant plaque or narrowing.
findings: Calcified / soft plaque at the [right] ICA origin.
Carotid web: shelf-like intraluminal projection along the posterior wall of the ICA bulb.
Floating thrombus in the ICA.

steps.label: Residual lumen and distal calibre
steps.detail: Assess the degree of stenosis, near-occlusion and the calibre of the distal ICA.
steps.look: Minimum lumen diameter compared with the normal distal ICA (NASCET method).
steps.normal: No haemodynamically significant stenosis.
findings: [Right] ICA stenosis of __% (NASCET).
Near-occlusion: severe stenosis with collapse of the distal ICA (not graded as a percentage).
steps.tip: Near-occlusion with distal collapse is a separate category; a percentage stenosis is misleading.

steps.label: Occlusion pattern
steps.detail: Describe the stump, length of occlusion and distal reconstitution.
steps.look: Delayed images to separate true occlusion from slow flow (pseudo-occlusion).
steps.normal: No occlusion.
findings: Occlusion of the [left] ICA from the origin with reconstitution of the [petrous / cavernous] segment.
Pseudo-occlusion: slow antegrade filling on delayed images.
steps.tip: Slow flow can mimic occlusion on a single early phase; check delayed images.

steps.label: Non-atherosclerotic causes
steps.detail: Look for dissection, fibromuscular dysplasia or other vasculopathy.
steps.look: Crescentic mural haematoma (fat-suppressed T1 on MRI), flap, tapered narrowing sparing the bulb.
steps.normal: No dissection or other vasculopathy.
findings: Dissection of the [left] ICA with crescentic mural haematoma and tapered narrowing distal to the bulb.
String-of-beads appearance (fibromuscular dysplasia).
steps.tip: Dissection usually spares the bulb and starts 2–3 cm above the bifurcation.

steps.label: Intracranial run-off and comparison
steps.detail: Assess the intracranial vessels within coverage, the contralateral side and interval change.
steps.look: Circle of Willis collaterals; the prior study.
steps.normal: Normal intracranial run-off; contralateral carotid normal.
findings: Tandem intracranial stenosis of the [ ].
Progression from __% to __% since [date].

steps.label: Global and regional atrophy
steps.detail: Describe global cortical atrophy and any regional predominance, symmetry and age appropriateness.
steps.look: Axial FLAIR and 3D T1 in three planes; GCA scale 0–3; posterior atrophy (Koedam) on sagittal and coronal images.
steps.normal: Brain volume appropriate for age.
findings: Global cortical atrophy, GCA [2].
Asymmetric frontal and anterior temporal atrophy (frontotemporal lobar degeneration pattern).
Posterior parietal and precuneus atrophy (Koedam [2]).

steps.label: Medial temporal lobe atrophy
steps.detail: Assess both hippocampi on comparable coronal planes with the MTA score.
steps.look: Coronal T1 through the hippocampal body at the level of the pons.
steps.normal: MTA score right 0/4, left 0/4.
findings: MTA right __/4, left __/4 (abnormal for age).
Asymmetric hippocampal atrophy, [left] greater than [right].
steps.tip: An MTA score of 2 or more under 75 years, or 3 or more at 75 and above, is usually considered abnormal.

steps.label: Vascular burden
steps.detail: Record white-matter disease (Fazekas), lacunes and strategic or territorial infarcts.
steps.look: FLAIR for white-matter lesions and lacunes; strategic sites: thalamus, caudate, angular gyrus.
steps.normal: No significant white-matter disease (Fazekas 0–1); no infarcts.
findings: Confluent white-matter hyperintensities, Fazekas 3.
Lacunes in the basal ganglia and thalami.
Strategic infarct in the [left thalamus].

steps.label: Microbleeds and siderosis
steps.detail: Describe microbleed number and distribution and cortical superficial siderosis.
steps.look: Susceptibility-weighted or T2* images.
steps.normal: No microbleeds or superficial siderosis.
findings: __ lobar microbleeds with cortical superficial siderosis (cerebral amyloid angiopathy pattern).
Deep microbleeds in the basal ganglia and pons (hypertensive pattern).
steps.tip: Lobar microbleeds and superficial siderosis suggest amyloid angiopathy and matter for anti-amyloid treatment eligibility.

steps.label: Treatable and alternative causes
steps.detail: Exclude mass, subdural collection, hydrocephalus, acute diffusion abnormality and other structural causes.
steps.look: DWI for cortical ribbon and deep grey restriction; ventricles versus sulci; subdural spaces.
steps.normal: No mass, collection, hydrocephalus or diffusion abnormality.
findings: Ventriculomegaly disproportionate to sulcal widening with tight high-convexity sulci (normal pressure hydrocephalus pattern).
Cortical ribbon and deep grey diffusion restriction (Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease pattern).
Chronic subdural haematoma.
steps.tip: Rapidly progressive symptoms need a different differential, including Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease.

steps.label: Meningeal and cranial nerve enhancement
steps.detail: Separate pachymeningeal (dural) from leptomeningeal enhancement and note cranial nerve enhancement.
steps.look: Post-contrast FLAIR and T1: dural enhancement follows the inner table; leptomeningeal enhancement enters sulci and cisterns.
steps.normal: No abnormal meningeal or cranial nerve enhancement.
findings: Smooth diffuse pachymeningeal enhancement (e.g., intracranial hypotension, post-operative).
Nodular leptomeningeal enhancement along the [cerebellar folia / basal cisterns].
Enhancement of the [ ] cranial nerve.
steps.tip: Pachymeningeal enhancement follows the skull; leptomeningeal enhancement dips into the sulci.

steps.label: Parenchymal lesions
steps.detail: Characterise the pattern — ring, nodular, gyral, perivascular — with central diffusion and surrounding FLAIR.
steps.look: Post-contrast T1 with DWI/ADC and FLAIR.
steps.normal: No enhancing parenchymal lesion.
findings: Smooth thin ring enhancement with central restricted diffusion (abscess pattern).
Incomplete (open) ring enhancement (demyelination pattern).
Gyral enhancement of the [ ] cortex (subacute infarct / encephalitis).
Punctate and curvilinear perivascular enhancement in the pons (CLIPPERS pattern).
steps.tip: An open ring facing the cortex suggests demyelination; a complete smooth ring with restricted diffusion suggests abscess.

steps.label: Extra-axial collections
steps.detail: Identify subdural or epidural collections, their thickness and diffusion.
steps.look: DWI for empyema; adjacent sinuses and bone.
steps.normal: No extra-axial collection.
findings: Subdural empyema along the [left] convexity, __ mm thick, with restricted diffusion.
Epidural collection adjacent to the [frontal sinus].

steps.label: Ventricles and CSF
steps.detail: Inspect ependymal enhancement, intraventricular debris and hydrocephalus.
steps.look: Dependent layering debris on DWI and FLAIR; ependymal surfaces.
steps.normal: No ependymal enhancement, debris or hydrocephalus.
findings: Ependymal enhancement with dependent debris (ventriculitis).
Hydrocephalus with obstruction at the [ ].

steps.label: Vascular complications and source
steps.detail: Check infarction, haemorrhage and venous or arterial complications, and look for a sinus, mastoid or operative source.
steps.look: Venous sinuses; arteries at the skull base; paranasal sinuses and mastoids.
steps.normal: No infarct, haemorrhage or vascular complication; no source identified.
findings: Venous sinus thrombosis adjacent to [mastoiditis].
Infarcts from vasculitis in the [ ].
Source: [frontal sinusitis / otomastoiditis / operative bed].

steps.label: Hippocampi
steps.detail: Compare hippocampal size, signal and internal architecture bilaterally.
steps.look: High-resolution coronal T2 perpendicular to the hippocampal long axis; 3D FLAIR.
steps.normal: Hippocampi symmetric with normal size, signal and internal architecture.
findings: [Left] hippocampal sclerosis: volume loss, increased T2/FLAIR signal and loss of internal architecture.
Atrophy of the ipsilateral fornix and mammillary body.
steps.tip: Look at the whole brain even after finding hippocampal sclerosis: dual pathology is common.

steps.label: Cortex and neuronal migration
steps.detail: Inspect cortical thickness, sulcation, grey–white junction, heterotopia and transmantle signal.
steps.look: 3D T1 and 3D FLAIR in all planes; compare with the other hemisphere.
steps.normal: Normal cortical thickness and grey–white junction; no heterotopia.
findings: Blurring of the grey–white junction with cortical thickening and a transmantle sign in the [right] [frontal] lobe (focal cortical dysplasia type II pattern).
Subependymal nodular heterotopia along the [ ] ventricle.
Polymicrogyria of the [ ].
steps.tip: The transmantle sign — a funnel of FLAIR signal from the cortex towards the ventricle — indicates focal cortical dysplasia type IIb.

steps.label: Focal lesions
steps.detail: Look for tumours, vascular malformations, gliosis and encephalomalacia.
steps.look: Susceptibility images for cavernomas; post-contrast images when acquired.
steps.normal: No tumour, vascular malformation or gliosis.
findings: Cavernoma __ mm in the [ ] with a haemosiderin rim.
Cortically based cystic lesion (DNET / ganglioglioma pattern).
Post-traumatic encephalomalacia and gliosis in the [ ].

steps.label: Temporal encephalocele and dual pathology
steps.detail: Look for temporal encephalocele, prior injury and any second relevant lesion.
steps.look: Coronal and sagittal images of the middle cranial fossa floor.
steps.normal: No encephalocele; no second lesion.
findings: Temporal pole encephalocele through a middle cranial fossa defect.
Second lesion: [ ] in addition to hippocampal sclerosis.

steps.label: Electroclinical concordance
steps.detail: Relate the lesion to the supplied EEG and semiology localisation without assuming causality, and consider peri-ictal change.
steps.look: Supplied EEG and semiology; the timing of the last seizure.
steps.normal: No peri-ictal change. No structural lesion; this does not exclude epilepsy.
findings: Lesion concordant with the supplied [left temporal] EEG focus.
Transient cortical and hippocampal diffusion and FLAIR change, compatible with peri-ictal change; follow-up to confirm resolution.
steps.tip: A normal MRI does not exclude epilepsy or subtle focal cortical dysplasia.

steps.label: Extra-axial haemorrhage
steps.detail: Distinguish epidural, subdural and subarachnoid haemorrhage.
steps.look: Brain window and a wider subdural window; epidural is biconvex and limited by sutures; subdural is crescentic and crosses sutures.
steps.normal: No extra-axial haemorrhage.
findings: Biconvex epidural haematoma over the [right temporal] convexity, __ mm thick, with an overlying fracture.
Crescentic acute subdural haematoma over the [left] convexity, __ mm thick.
Traumatic subarachnoid haemorrhage in the [ ] sulci.
steps.tip: An epidural haematoma does not cross sutures; a subdural haematoma does not cross the midline.

steps.label: Parenchymal injury
steps.detail: Assess contusions, intraparenchymal haematoma and oedema.
steps.look: Frontal and temporal poles and inferior surfaces (coup and contrecoup sites).
steps.normal: No contusion or intraparenchymal haemorrhage.
findings: Haemorrhagic contusions of the [inferior frontal / anterior temporal] lobes.
Petechial haemorrhages at the grey–white junction and corpus callosum (diffuse axonal injury pattern).
steps.tip: Contusions often enlarge on early follow-up CT.

steps.label: Ventricles
steps.detail: Identify intraventricular blood and ventricular obstruction.
steps.look: Occipital horns for layering blood; ventricular size.
steps.normal: No intraventricular haemorrhage; ventricles normal.
findings: Intraventricular blood layering in the occipital horns.
Early hydrocephalus.

steps.label: Mass effect
steps.detail: Measure midline shift and assess the basal cisterns and herniation.
steps.look: Midline shift at the level of the septum pellucidum; ambient and quadrigeminal cisterns.
steps.normal: No midline shift; basal cisterns patent.
findings: Midline shift of __ mm to the [left].
Effaced basal cisterns with uncal herniation.
Duret haemorrhage in the pons (secondary to descending herniation).

steps.label: Skull and comparison
steps.detail: Review skull and skull-base fractures, pneumocephalus and interval change.
steps.look: Bone window with multiplanar and 3D reformats.
steps.normal: No skull fracture or pneumocephalus.
findings: Fracture of the [right temporal] bone crossing the middle meningeal groove.
Skull-base fracture with pneumocephalus.
Increase in contusion size since [time].

steps.label: Compartment
steps.detail: Identify parenchymal, subarachnoid, subdural and intraventricular blood.
steps.look: Non-contrast CT brain window; each compartment in turn.
steps.normal: No intracranial haemorrhage.
findings: Intraparenchymal haemorrhage in the [ ].
Diffuse subarachnoid haemorrhage in the basal cisterns.

steps.label: Distribution and size
steps.detail: Describe lobar, deep or posterior-fossa location, size and perihaematomal oedema.
steps.look: Measure three axes (ABC/2 for volume); spot sign on CTA.
findings: Deep haemorrhage in the [left] putamen, __ × __ × __ mm (hypertensive pattern).
Lobar haemorrhage in the [ ] (amyloid angiopathy, vascular malformation or tumour to be considered).
Cerebellar haemorrhage __ mm.
steps.tip: Deep haemorrhage in an older hypertensive patient is typical; a lobar or young-patient haemorrhage needs a search for a cause.

steps.label: Subarachnoid and ventricular blood
steps.detail: Map cisternal and sulcal blood and intraventricular extension.
steps.look: Basal cisterns, Sylvian fissures, interhemispheric fissure, convexity sulci and ventricles.
steps.normal: No subarachnoid or intraventricular blood.
findings: Diffuse basal cisternal SAH (aneurysmal pattern).
Perimesencephalic SAH confined to the cisterns anterior to the brainstem.
Convexity SAH in a few sulci.
Intraventricular extension.
steps.tip: Perimesencephalic SAH is usually non-aneurysmal, but CTA is still needed.

steps.label: Mass effect and hydrocephalus
steps.detail: Assess ventricular obstruction, shift and cisterns.
steps.look: Temporal horns for early hydrocephalus; midline; basal cisterns.
steps.normal: No hydrocephalus or mass effect.
findings: Acute hydrocephalus with dilated temporal horns.
Midline shift __ mm.
Effacement of the basal cisterns.

steps.label: Underlying cause
steps.detail: Describe any vascular or structural cause demonstrated and what remains unassessed.
steps.look: CTA or MRA for aneurysm, AVM or fistula; MRI for tumour, cavernoma and amyloid angiopathy.
steps.normal: No underlying vascular lesion on CTA.
findings: Aneurysm of the [anterior communicating artery], __ mm.
Arteriovenous malformation with nidus in the [ ].
Spot sign within the haematoma (risk of expansion).
Underlying cause not yet evaluated.

steps.label: Brain lesion distribution
steps.detail: Describe periventricular, cortical or juxtacortical, infratentorial and callosal lesions and their morphology.
steps.look: Sagittal 3D FLAIR for callosal lesions; axial FLAIR and T2; lesions perpendicular to the ventricles.
steps.normal: No white-matter lesions typical of demyelination.
findings: Ovoid periventricular lesions perpendicular to the lateral ventricles and involving the callosal undersurface.
Juxtacortical lesions in the [ ].
Infratentorial lesions in the [pons / middle cerebellar peduncle].
steps.tip: Non-specific punctate white-matter foci are not enough for MS; look for the typical locations and morphology.

steps.label: Spinal cord and optic nerves
steps.detail: Report cord lesions by level, length and axial position, and optic nerve findings when imaged.
steps.look: Sagittal and axial cord images; fat-suppressed coronal optic nerve images.
steps.normal: Spinal cord and optic nerves not imaged / normal.
findings: Short-segment (under two vertebral segments) peripheral cord lesion at [C3].
Longitudinally extensive cord lesion over __ segments (consider NMOSD or MOGAD).
Optic nerve [T2 signal / enhancement].
steps.tip: A longitudinally extensive cord lesion is atypical for MS.

steps.label: Interval activity
steps.detail: Count unequivocally new or enlarging T2 lesions and enhancing lesions against a named comparison.
steps.look: Matched FLAIR with the comparison study; post-contrast T1 when given.
steps.normal: No new or enlarging T2 lesions and no enhancing lesions compared with [date].
findings: __ new T2 lesions in the [ ] compared with [date].
__ enhancing lesions.

steps.label: Central vein sign and rim lesions
steps.detail: Report the central vein sign and paramagnetic rim lesions only when a suitable sequence was acquired.
steps.look: Susceptibility-weighted or FLAIR* images.
steps.normal: Susceptibility markers not assessed.
findings: Central vein sign present in __ of __ assessed lesions.
Paramagnetic rim lesions: [number, sites].

steps.label: Mimics and atypical features
steps.detail: Consider small-vessel disease, migraine, infection and alternative inflammatory patterns, and list atypical features.
steps.look: Lesion location and shape; diffusion and haemorrhage; cortex and deep grey matter.
steps.normal: No features to suggest an alternative diagnosis.
findings: Punctate subcortical lesions sparing the callosum and periventricular regions (small-vessel pattern).
Large confluent lesions with deep grey involvement (ADEM / MOGAD pattern).
Area postrema lesion (NMOSD context).

steps.label: Gland and lesion epicentre
steps.detail: Identify whether the lesion arises from the gland, stalk or an extrasellar structure, and measure it.
steps.look: Small-field coronal and sagittal T1 and T2; dynamic images for microadenoma when acquired.
steps.normal: Normal pituitary gland; no focal lesion.
findings: Microadenoma __ mm in the [right] gland with delayed enhancement.
Macroadenoma __ × __ × __ mm with a snowman (figure-of-eight) configuration.
Non-enhancing midline cyst between the anterior and posterior lobe (Rathke cleft cyst pattern).
steps.tip: Find the normal gland first: a lesion separate from the gland is not a pituitary adenoma.

steps.label: Signal and enhancement
steps.detail: Describe T1 and T2 signal, enhancement, haemorrhage, calcification and cystic change.
steps.look: T1 pre-contrast for haemorrhage and proteinaceous content; post-contrast images.
findings: T1-hyperintense haemorrhage within the macroadenoma (apoplexy in the appropriate clinical setting).
Mixed solid-cystic suprasellar mass with calcification (craniopharyngioma pattern).
Homogeneous enhancement with a dural tail (meningioma pattern).

steps.label: Stalk and suprasellar region
steps.detail: Assess stalk position and thickness, posterior pituitary bright spot and suprasellar extension.
steps.look: Sagittal and coronal images of the stalk and hypothalamus.
steps.normal: Stalk midline and normal in thickness; posterior pituitary bright spot present.
findings: Stalk deviated to the [left].
Thickened stalk __ mm with absent posterior bright spot (germinoma, histiocytosis or hypophysitis to be considered).
Suprasellar extension to the hypothalamus.

steps.label: Optic chiasm and nerves
steps.detail: Describe the relationship to the chiasm and optic nerves.
steps.look: Coronal T2 through the chiasm.
steps.normal: Optic chiasm clear.
findings: Lesion contacts and elevates the optic chiasm.
Compression of the chiasm with T2 signal change.

steps.label: Cavernous sinus and skull base
steps.detail: Describe cavernous sinus invasion, carotid encasement, sellar floor, sphenoid sinus and vascular mimics.
steps.look: Coronal images: tumour lateral to the lateral tangent of the carotid, or encasing more than two-thirds of it, suggests invasion.
steps.normal: No cavernous sinus invasion; sellar floor intact; no vascular lesion.
findings: [Right] cavernous sinus invasion with carotid encasement (Knosp grade __).
Erosion of the sellar floor into the sphenoid sinus.
Flow void in the lesion: aneurysm must be excluded.
steps.tip: Exclude an aneurysm before any transsphenoidal biopsy of a parasellar mass.

steps.label: Dural sinuses
steps.detail: Assess each named dural sinus for patency or thrombus.
steps.look: Non-contrast CT for dense clot or cord sign; CTV or contrast MRV source images for filling defects and the empty delta sign.
steps.normal: Dural venous sinuses patent.
findings: Filling defect in the superior sagittal sinus (empty delta sign) extending to the [right transverse and sigmoid] sinuses.
Hyperdense [left transverse] sinus on non-contrast CT (dense clot sign).
steps.tip: A hypoplastic transverse sinus or arachnoid granulation is a common mimic; check the source images.

steps.label: Deep and cortical veins
steps.detail: Inspect the deep venous system and cortical veins.
steps.look: Internal cerebral veins, vein of Galen and straight sinus; cortical veins on susceptibility images.
steps.normal: Deep and cortical veins patent.
findings: Thrombosis of the internal cerebral veins and straight sinus.
Isolated cortical vein thrombosis (cord sign / susceptibility blooming).

steps.label: Parenchymal effects
steps.detail: Assess oedema, venous infarction and haemorrhage that do not follow arterial territories.
steps.look: FLAIR and DWI; susceptibility for haemorrhage.
steps.normal: No parenchymal oedema, infarction or haemorrhage.
findings: Venous oedema / infarction in the [ ] crossing arterial territories.
Bilateral thalamic oedema (deep venous thrombosis).
Haemorrhagic venous infarct __ mm.
steps.tip: Parenchymal change that does not match an arterial territory, especially with haemorrhage, should prompt venous imaging.

steps.label: Mass effect
steps.detail: Review swelling, ventricles and herniation.
steps.look: Midline, ventricles and basal cisterns.
steps.normal: No mass effect.
findings: Swelling with __ mm midline shift.
Effaced basal cisterns.

steps.label: Mimics and comparison
steps.detail: Distinguish hypoplasia, arachnoid granulations and technical signal loss, and compare patency over time.
steps.look: Contrast-enhanced source images rather than time-of-flight alone.
steps.normal: No mimic; not applicable.
findings: Hypoplastic [left] transverse sinus without thrombus.
Arachnoid granulation: rounded CSF-density filling defect.
Partial recanalisation since [date].
steps.tip: Time-of-flight signal loss alone is not evidence of thrombosis.

steps.label: Alignment
steps.detail: Assess craniocervical and subaxial alignment.
steps.look: Sagittal CT: anterior vertebral, posterior vertebral, spinolaminar and spinous process lines; basion–dens and atlanto-dental intervals.
steps.normal: Normal craniocervical and subaxial alignment.
findings: Anterolisthesis of [C5] on [C6] by __ mm.
Widened basion–dens interval (atlanto-occipital dissociation to be considered).
Loss of the spinolaminar line at [ ].

steps.label: Fractures
steps.detail: Describe fracture level, morphology, displacement and posterior element involvement.
steps.look: Axial, sagittal and coronal CT; C1 ring, odontoid, C2 pars and each subaxial level.
steps.normal: No cervical spine fracture.
findings: Type [II] odontoid fracture with __ mm displacement.
Bilateral C2 pars fractures (hangman fracture).
Jefferson fracture of the C1 ring with lateral mass offset.
Flexion teardrop fracture of [C5].

steps.label: Facet joints and ligaments
steps.detail: Assess the facets and signs of ligament disruption.
steps.look: Sagittal images through each facet column; MRI STIR for ligaments when acquired.
steps.normal: Facets aligned; no evidence of ligament injury.
findings: Unilateral facet dislocation at [C5–C6] on the [right] (perched / locked).
Bilateral facet dislocation at [ ].
MRI: disruption of the posterior ligamentous complex / anterior longitudinal ligament.
steps.tip: A jumped facet appears as a "naked facet" on axial images and as a locked facet on the sagittal facet column.

steps.label: Canal and cord
steps.detail: Describe canal compromise and cord signal when MRI is available.
steps.look: Axial CT for bone fragments in the canal; sagittal MRI T2 and STIR for the cord.
steps.normal: Canal preserved; cord normal where imaged.
findings: Retropulsed fragment narrowing the canal to __ mm.
Cord oedema from [C4] to [C6] [with haemorrhage].
Epidural haematoma compressing the cord.

steps.label: Soft tissues and associated injury
steps.detail: Review prevertebral swelling and features that need vascular assessment.
steps.look: Prevertebral soft tissue thickness; foramina transversaria; other injuries.
steps.normal: No prevertebral swelling; foramina transversaria intact.
findings: Prevertebral soft-tissue swelling at [C2–C6].
Fracture through the [right] foramen transversarium: vertebral artery injury should be assessed with CTA.
Associated injury: [ ].
steps.tip: A fracture through the foramen transversarium or a subluxation should prompt vertebral artery assessment.

steps.label: Numbering and alignment
steps.detail: Establish the numbering reference and transitional anatomy, and describe alignment.
steps.look: Count from a documented reference (sacrum or C2 localiser); sagittal T1 and T2.
steps.normal: Normal lumbar lordosis; five lumbar vertebrae without transitional anatomy.
findings: Lumbosacral transitional vertebra; numbering based on [ ].
Degenerative anterolisthesis of [L4] on [L5] (grade 1).
steps.tip: State how you counted: an error in numbering leads to surgery at the wrong level.

steps.label: Discs
steps.detail: Describe disc height and signal, and bulge or herniation using the 2.0 nomenclature.
steps.look: Sagittal and axial T2 at each level: bulge (over 25% of the circumference), protrusion, extrusion or sequestration.
steps.normal: Discs normal in height and signal; no herniation.
findings: [L4–L5]: [right paracentral] protrusion.
[L5–S1]: [left subarticular] extrusion migrating __ mm caudally.
Sequestrated fragment behind the [L5] body.
Modic type [1] endplate changes at [ ].
steps.tip: A bulge is diffuse (more than 25% of the circumference); a herniation is focal.

steps.label: Central canal and lateral recesses
steps.detail: Describe canal and lateral recess narrowing and the traversing root affected.
steps.look: Axial T2 at disc level; follow each traversing root in the lateral recess.
steps.normal: Central canal and lateral recesses patent; traversing roots free.
findings: [Right] subarticular recess stenosis compressing the traversing [L5] root.
Moderate central canal stenosis at [L4–L5] (facet and ligamentum flavum hypertrophy with bulge).
steps.tip: A paracentral herniation at L4–L5 affects the traversing L5 root.

steps.label: Foramina and extraforaminal zone
steps.detail: Assess the exiting roots in the foramina and beyond.
steps.look: Sagittal images through the foramina; axial images lateral to the pedicles.
steps.normal: Foramina patent; exiting roots free.
findings: [Left] foraminal herniation at [L4–L5] compressing the exiting [L4] root.
Severe [right] foraminal stenosis at [L5–S1].
steps.tip: A foraminal herniation at L4–L5 affects the exiting L4 root.

steps.label: Conus, cauda equina and other structures
steps.detail: Inspect the conus, cauda equina, facets, synovial cysts and other findings.
steps.look: Sagittal T2 to the conus; axial images of the facets.
steps.normal: Conus normal at [L1]; cauda equina normal; no other significant finding.
findings: Severe canal stenosis with crowding of the cauda equina.
Synovial cyst from the [right L4–L5] facet.
Epidural lipomatosis.

steps.label: Compression
steps.detail: First exclude extrinsic cord compression and canal disease.
steps.look: Sagittal T2 and axial images at every narrowed level.
steps.normal: No cord compression.
findings: Cord compression at [C5–C6] by disc–osteophyte complex with cord signal change (compressive myelopathy).
Epidural mass compressing the cord at [ ].
steps.tip: Always exclude compression before considering an intrinsic cord disease.

steps.label: Longitudinal extent
steps.detail: Map cord signal by level and length.
steps.look: Sagittal T2 and STIR; count vertebral segments.
steps.normal: No cord signal abnormality.
findings: Short-segment lesion (under two vertebral segments) at [ ].
Longitudinally extensive lesion from [ ] to [ ] (three or more segments).
Multifocal cord lesions.
steps.tip: Short peripheral lesions suggest MS; longitudinally extensive central lesions suggest NMOSD, MOGAD, ADEM or other causes.

steps.label: Axial pattern
steps.detail: Assess axial location and the proportion of the cord involved.
steps.look: Axial T2 through each lesion.
findings: Peripheral, dorsolateral lesion involving less than half of the cross-section (MS pattern).
Central grey matter involvement (owl-eye pattern: infarction, MOGAD).
Symmetric dorsal column involvement (metabolic pattern, e.g., B12 deficiency).

steps.label: Calibre and enhancement
steps.detail: Assess cord expansion, atrophy and enhancement.
steps.look: Sagittal and axial post-contrast T1.
steps.normal: Normal cord calibre; no enhancement.
findings: Cord expansion with heterogeneous enhancement (tumour pattern).
Patchy enhancement of the lesion.
Cord atrophy at [ ].

steps.label: Associated findings
steps.detail: Inspect perimedullary vessels, the conus and relevant brain findings.
steps.look: Dorsal surface of the cord for flow voids; brain if imaged.
steps.normal: No abnormal perimedullary vessels; conus normal.
findings: Dilated perimedullary veins on the dorsal cord with conus oedema (spinal dural arteriovenous fistula pattern).
Brain lesions typical of demyelination.
steps.tip: Flow voids on the dorsal cord surface with lower cord oedema suggest a spinal dural arteriovenous fistula.

steps.label: Levels and alignment
steps.detail: Identify all injured levels and alignment abnormalities.
steps.look: Sagittal CT reformats with a documented numbering reference.
steps.normal: Normal thoracolumbar alignment.
findings: Fracture at [T12], counted from [ ].
Kyphosis of __° at [ ].
Translation at [ ].

steps.label: Vertebral body morphology
steps.detail: Assess compression, burst components and the posterior wall.
steps.look: Sagittal and axial CT through the vertebral body.
steps.normal: No vertebral body fracture.
findings: Wedge compression fracture of [ ] with __% anterior height loss; posterior wall intact.
Burst fracture of [ ] with posterior wall retropulsion.
Vertical axial loading fracture (jumper pattern) of [L1].

steps.label: Posterior elements and ligaments
steps.detail: Review posterior elements, facets and ligament injury.
steps.look: Interspinous distance, facet alignment, horizontal fractures; MRI for ligaments.
steps.normal: Posterior elements and facets intact.
findings: Horizontal fracture through the posterior elements and body (Chance fracture).
Interspinous widening and facet diastasis (flexion-distraction injury).
steps.tip: A Chance fracture is a flexion-distraction injury, often with intra-abdominal injury (seat-belt mechanism).

steps.label: Canal and neural elements
steps.detail: Describe retropulsion and the neural assessment actually available.
steps.look: Axial CT for canal narrowing; MRI for cord, conus and epidural blood.
steps.normal: Canal preserved; cord and conus normal where imaged.
findings: Retropulsion of __ mm narrowing the canal by about __%.
Conus compression / signal change.
Epidural haematoma.

steps.label: Associated injuries
steps.detail: Identify other fractures and paraspinal or visceral injury.
steps.look: The whole imaged spine; paraspinal tissues; abdomen for seat-belt injuries.
steps.normal: No additional spinal fracture; no paraspinal or visceral injury.
findings: Non-contiguous fracture at [ ].
Paraspinal haematoma.
Associated bowel or mesenteric injury (seat-belt mechanism).

steps.label: Dura and veins
steps.detail: Assess diffuse pachymeningeal enhancement and venous engorgement.
steps.look: Post-contrast T1; sagittal and coronal images of the transverse sinuses (convex lower border).
steps.normal: No pachymeningeal enhancement; no venous engorgement.
findings: Smooth diffuse pachymeningeal enhancement.
Venous distension sign: convex inferior border of the dominant transverse sinus.
steps.tip: Diffuse smooth pachymeningeal enhancement with engorged sinuses is the typical cranial pattern.

steps.label: Brain sagging
steps.detail: Review midbrain and brainstem sagging, the basal cisterns and tonsillar position.
steps.look: Midsagittal T1/T2: suprasellar and prepontine cisterns, mamillopontine distance, midbrain–pons angle, tonsils.
steps.normal: No brain sagging; basal cisterns normal.
findings: Sagging of the midbrain with reduced mamillopontine distance and effaced prepontine and suprasellar cisterns.
Low-lying cerebellar tonsils from brain sagging (not a congenital Chiari malformation).
steps.tip: Tonsillar descent from sagging should not be called a Chiari I malformation.

steps.label: Subdural collections
steps.detail: Describe subdural fluid or haematomas, their thickness and mass effect.
steps.look: FLAIR and T1 over both convexities.
steps.normal: No subdural collections.
findings: Bilateral subdural hygromas, up to __ mm.
Subdural haematoma with mass effect.

steps.label: Pituitary and supportive findings
steps.detail: Assess pituitary engorgement and whether the findings fit together.
steps.look: Sagittal images of the pituitary.
steps.normal: Pituitary normal; no additional supportive findings.
findings: Enlarged hyperaemic pituitary gland.
Findings together give a [high / intermediate / low] Bern score probability.
steps.tip: The Bern score combines these cranial signs to estimate the likelihood of a spinal CSF leak.

steps.label: Spinal assessment
steps.detail: Describe spinal extradural fluid and leak site only if the spine was studied.
steps.look: Heavily T2-weighted fat-suppressed spine MRI; dynamic myelography for localisation.
steps.normal: Spine not imaged.
findings: Spinal extradural fluid from [ ] to [ ] (ventral dural tear likely).
Meningeal diverticulum at [ ].
No extradural collection; CSF-venous fistula not excluded.
steps.tip: A normal brain MRI does not exclude a spinal CSF leak.
